s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive weight loss with a palpable abdominal mass and anemia
salient_findings: Palpable mass in the right iliac fossa
Drop in hemoglobin from 13 g/dL to 10 g/dL
key_facts: 52-year-old woman with well-controlled HIV
Viral load <40 copies/mL
CD4 count 290 cells/mm3
20% weight loss (12 kg) over one year
Initial weight loss was intentional but accelerated in recent months
No fevers, night sweats, gastrointestinal symptoms, or gynecological complaints
Palpable mass in the right iliac fossa
Drop in hemoglobin from 13 g/dL to 10 g/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase level of 643 U/L
C-reactive protein level of 80 mg/L
Normal white-cell count
History of hysterectomy for micro-invasive cervical carcinoma in 2002
CT scan showed a 15 cm mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall
Potential fistulous connection to the cecum
Mesenteric lymph nodes measuring up to 27 mm
No distant metastases
Serum tumor markers (CA19-9, CEA, CA125) were all negative

shortlist.label: Cervical cancer recurrence

shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal mass and elevated lactate dehydrogenase level

raw.rationale: History of micro-invasive cervical carcinoma and presence of a large mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall with a potential fistulous connection to the cecum, suggesting local recurrence and invasion

rejected.label: Vaginal cancer
rejected.why: While possible, the history of cervical cancer makes recurrence more likely

rejected.label: Ovarian cancer
rejected.why: No specific evidence of ovarian involvement and negative serum tumor markers

rejected.label: Colorectal cancer
rejected.why: The mass is described as possibly arising from the vaginal wall, not the colon, and the fistulous connection to the cecum could be secondary to the primary vaginal/vulvar process

rejected.label: Carcinosarcoma of the vagina
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor and the clinical presentation and history are more suggestive of a recurrence of the previously diagnosed cervical cancer
